review_candidates.title: Event Coordinator
review_candidates.description: Position Overview The Event Coordinator is responsible for planning, organizing, coordinating, and supporting events from initial requirements through execution and post-event evaluation. The role manages event logistics, schedules, suppliers, venues, guest arrangements, budgets, event materials, and on-site activities to ensure events are delivered smoothly and professionally. The position works closely with clients, internal teams, venues, vendors, contractors, speakers, entertainers, sponsors, and other stakeholders to coordinate all operational requirements. The Event Coordinator may support a wide range of events including corporate functions, conferences, exhibitions, product launches, promotional campaigns, weddings, private functions, networking events, and special occasions. Key Responsibilities Understand client or internal stakeholder requirements, event objectives, target audience, budget, theme, schedule, and expected outcomes. Develop detailed event plans covering timelines, venues, suppliers, staffing, guest arrangements, logistics, equipment, activities, and deliverables. Prepare event proposals, quotations, budgets, schedules, checklists, floor plans, run sheets, and other planning documentation. Research, evaluate, and coordinate suitable venues based on capacity, location, accessibility, facilities, cost, layout, and event requirements. Coordinate with caterers, decorators, AV providers, photographers, videographers, entertainers, transport providers, security teams, printers, production companies, and other suppliers. Obtain and compare supplier quotations and assist with commercial negotiations to ensure requirements are met within approved budgets. Manage supplier bookings, purchase orders, contracts, deposits, delivery schedules, and service requirements. Maintain regular communication with clients and stakeholders and provide updates regarding event progress, changes, and outstanding requirements. Coordinate guest lists, invitations, RSVPs, registrations, seating arrangements, VIP requirements, badges, tickets, welcome materials, and attendee communications. Coordinate speakers, presenters, performers, hosts, sponsors, exhibitors, VIP guests, and other participants. Prepare event schedules, programmes, briefing documents, contact lists, production schedules, and event-day run sheets. Coordinate event setup, including furniture, decorations, signage, lighting, audio-visual equipment, registration areas, catering arrangements, branding materials, and other requirements. Conduct venue inspections and site visits to identify logistical requirements, potential issues, access limitations, and operational risks. Work with venue and supplier teams to ensure setup and preparation are completed according to agreed specifications and timelines. Monitor event budgets, expenses, supplier costs, payments, deposits, and outstanding invoices to maintain financial control. Maintain accurate records of event-related quotations, contracts, invoices, guest information, schedules, supplier details, and approvals. Coordinate event-day operations and ensure suppliers, staff, guests, speakers, and other stakeholders are in the appropriate locations at the required times. Monitor event schedules and ensure programmes, presentations, catering, entertainment, registration, and other activities remain on schedule. Provide on-site support and respond quickly to operational issues, client requests, guest concerns, supplier problems, and unexpected changes. Coordinate event staff, temporary workers, promoters, volunteers, registration teams, and other personnel where required. Brief event staff and suppliers regarding responsibilities, schedules, safety requirements, customer-service expectations, and operational procedures. Ensure event branding, signage, promotional materials, displays, and other visual elements are correctly positioned and presented. Support event marketing and promotional activities through social media, email communications, invitations, digital content, partnerships, and promotional materials where applicable. Coordinate transportation, accommodation, equipment delivery, storage, access arrangements, and other event logistics when required. Ensure events comply with company policies, venue requirements, health and safety procedures, security requirements, permits, and applicable regulations. Maintain professional relationships with clients, venues, suppliers, contractors, partners, and other stakeholders. Handle client feedback and complaints professionally and escalate significant issues to management when appropriate. Assist with event breakdown, equipment collection, supplier departure, venue restoration, and post-event requirements. Reconcile event expenses and ensure outstanding financial and administrative matters are completed after each event. Collect attendee, client, supplier, and team feedback and prepare post-event reports highlighting outcomes, issues, and improvement opportunities. Review event performance against objectives, attendance, budget, guest experience, operational efficiency, and other relevant KPIs. Maintain an organized database of suppliers, venues, event contacts, quotations, pricing information, and previous event records. Support multiple events simultaneously while maintaining accurate timelines, communication, documentation, and operational priorities. Requirements Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Event Management, Hospitality Management, Marketing, Communications, Business Administration, Tourism, Public Relations, or a related field. Proven experience in event coordination, event planning, hospitality, marketing, exhibitions, conferences, weddings, corporate events, or a related environment. Strong understanding of event planning, logistics, venue coordination, supplier management, guest management, and on-site event execution. Experience coordinating vendors, contractors, venues, caterers, AV suppliers, production teams, or other event service providers. Strong organizational and multitasking skills with the ability to manage multiple deadlines, suppliers, stakeholders, and event requirements. Excellent communication, interpersonal, negotiation, coordination, and client-service skills. Strong problem-solving ability and the ability to remain calm and professional under pressure. Good understanding of event budgeting, quotation comparison, expense tracking, and basic financial administration. Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Experience with event-management, registration, CRM, project-management, or scheduling platforms is an advantage. Strong attention to detail and ability to identify potential operational issues before and during events. Creative mindset with the ability to contribute ideas for event themes, experiences, activities, branding, and guest engagement. Ability to work independently while coordinating effectively with internal teams and external stakeholders. Strong time-management and prioritization skills in a fast-paced environment. Professional appearance and customer-focused approach when representing the company at events. Willingness to work evenings, weekends, public holidays, extended hours, and event-day shifts when required. Willingness to travel to venues, exhibitions, conferences, and other event locations when required. Additional language skills are an advantage, particularly when working with international clients, guests, suppliers, or corporate events.

review_candidates.description: About the Role: Reporting to the Area Maintenance Manager, the Electrical Section Head will be responsible for leading the Electrical maintenance discipline (LV/MV power distribution, lighting, standby power/UPS, and building electrical systems) for the maintained assets (Level 1 & 2 facility maintenance) across stations, depot and service points on the high-speed railway project in Egypt. This role ensures that field execution, technical supervision, and workforce planning for the Electrical section are strictly aligned with the approved Preventive Maintenance Plans, ERA Common Safety Method risk requirements, and ISO 55000:2024. By providing technical authority over the Electrical discipline and coordinating closely with the Planning & Scheduling Office and Warehouse & Inventory teams, this role guarantees safe, reliable, and compliant electrical asset performance. Key Responsibilities: Establish and maintain discipline-specific maintenance standards, procedures, and work instructions; review and approve all maintenance method statements, risk assessments, and technical reports. Provide technical leadership on complex fault diagnosis, corrective work scoping, and maintenance strategy, ensuring alignment with OEM requirements, applicable codes, and statutory obligations. Oversee the execution and quality of preventive and corrective maintenance across all discipline-maintained assets, reviewing quality and signing off on significant maintenance interventions. Monitor discipline asset performance data and work with the Asset Strategy function on FMECA, CBM, and maintenance optimization; escalate recurring failures and major asset condition issues. Plan and manage the discipline workforce (Engineers, Supervisors, Technicians), coordinate resourcing with the Planning & Scheduling Sr. Engineer, and identify training and competence gaps. Manage discipline-specific tooling and PPE requirements in coordination with the Warehouse & Tooling function. Ensure all discipline maintenance records, WO close-outs, and defect reports are accurately entered in the CMMS; maintain as-maintained technical files and support statutory inspection scheduling and closure. Where facility maintenance is subcontracted, act as the technical authority: review and approve subcontractor method statements and risk assessments, conduct quality surveillance inspections, and review and accept work order close-out records before CMMS entry. Retain Permit-to-Work authority over all subcontractor activities within the discipline, and formally record and escalate subcontractor non-conformances, quality failures, and safety violations. Participate in cross-network technical coordination forums, share lessons learned and procedure updates with counterpart Discipline Section Heads and contribute discipline-specific content to the monthly maintenance performance report. Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering — required. Minimum 10 years of total experience in electrical/facility maintenance, including minimum 5 years in a supervisory or section head role on a major infrastructure or transport project. Strong technical knowledge of LV/MV power distribution, lighting, standby power/UPS, and building electrical systems. Demonstrated experience leading a maintenance team through a mobilization phase, including PM programm rollout — preferred given the current project phase. Working knowledge of ISO 55000:2024 / ISO 55001 asset management principles and BS EN 13460/ISO 14224 maintenance documentation practices. Familiarity with the ERA Common Safety Method for risk evaluation and assessment. Prior exposure to rail, metro, airport, or similarly regulated infrastructure environment — preferred. Proven experience managing OEM/EPC interfaces for equipment defects, warranty, and technical support. Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to manage multiple sites simultaneously during a compressed mobilization timeline. Good command of written and spoken English; Arabic is an advantage.

review_candidates.description: Commissioning Lead 📍 Kvandal, Norway Join CTS Group and Help Deliver the Next Generation of Digital Infrastructure CTS Group is a fast-growing international design and build company specialising in data centre development across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA). With over 40 nationalities represented across our teams, we foster a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performance culture where technical expertise and innovation drive every project. As we continue to expand our hyperscale data centre portfolio, we are seeking an experienced and technically strong Commissioning Lead to join our project team in Kvandal, Norway . This is a critical role within one of our mission-critical projects, responsible for ensuring the successful transition from construction to fully operational facility handover. Working closely with project leadership, engineering teams, clients, subcontractors, and commissioning partners, you will drive commissioning excellence across all mechanical, electrical, controls, and life safety systems. The Role As Commissioning Lead, you will take ownership of commissioning planning, coordination, execution, and reporting activities throughout the project lifecycle. You will be instrumental in ensuring all systems perform reliably, safely, and efficiently before client handover, supporting CTS's commitment to delivering world-class data centre facilities. This role requires strong technical knowledge, exceptional organisational skills, and the ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders in a fast-paced, mission-critical construction environment. Key Responsibilities Commissioning Leadership Lead and manage all commissioning activities from pre-functional testing through functional performance testing and Integrated Systems Testing (IST). Develop and implement commissioning strategies aligned with CTS project delivery objectives. Drive system readiness, milestone achievement, and successful project handovers. Project Coordination Collaborate with construction, engineering, QA/QC, design, commissioning, and project management teams to ensure seamless delivery. Coordinate subcontractors, OEM vendors, specialist contractors, and third-party commissioning providers. Work closely with Mechanical, Electrical, CSA, BMS, EPMS, and Operations teams to manage system interfaces and dependencies. Client & Stakeholder Management Act as a key commissioning interface with clients and commissioning consultants. Coordinate test witnessing schedules and readiness reviews. Provide regular progress updates, risk assessments, and commissioning status reports to project leadership and client teams. Participate in design reviews, project meetings, and commissioning workshops. System Readiness & Testing Develop readiness plans and verify completion of all commissioning prerequisites, including: QA/QC sign-offs Equipment inspections Flushing and cleaning activities Energisation approvals Vendor start-up activities Support and oversee FATs, SATs, integrated testing, and witness testing of critical systems. Documentation & Reporting Manage commissioning documentation including: Pre-functional checklists Functional testing procedures Method statements Equipment start-up records Defect and issue logs Turnover documentation Track system readiness and test outcomes through commissioning management platforms and digital delivery tools. Ensure turnover packs and final handover documentation are completed to the highest standard. Safety & Quality Leadership Promote and uphold CTS's commitment to safety excellence and quality delivery. Ensure all commissioning activities are executed in accordance with site safety requirements and industry best practices. Participate in EHS, QA/QC, and project readiness meetings. Support the delivery of a zero-harm culture across all commissioning activities. What We're Looking For Qualifications Degree or Diploma in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Building Services Engineering, or a related discipline. Additional commissioning or data centre-related certifications are advantageous. Experience Minimum 5 years of commissioning experience within construction, engineering, or mission-critical environments. At least 2 years in a commissioning leadership role on a data centre, pharmaceutical, industrial, or other critical infrastructure project. Experience delivering commissioning activities on large-scale construction projects from installation through handover. Technical Knowledge Strong understanding of: Electrical distribution systems UPS and standby power systems HVAC and cooling infrastructure BMS and EPMS systems Fire detection and life safety systems Integrated Systems Testing (IST) Working knowledge of commissioning standards such as ASHRAE, BSRIA, and Uptime Institute methodologies. Experience using commissioning and project management platforms such as CxAlloy, CxPlanner, Procore, BIM 360, or equivalent. Personal Attributes Strong leadership and coordination capabilities. Highly organised with excellent attention to detail. Strong communication and stakeholder management skills. Proactive problem solver with a solutions-focused mindset. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced project environment. Why Join CTS Group? Work on one of Norway's most exciting hyperscale data centre developments. Join a rapidly growing international company at the forefront of digital infrastructure delivery. Collaborate with experienced professionals from over 40 nationalities. Play a key role in delivering cutting-edge mission-critical facilities for leading global clients. Enjoy career progression opportunities within a business experiencing significant international growth. Be part of a culture built on safety, innovation, accountability, and engineering excellence. Apply Today If you're passionate about commissioning complex mission-critical systems and want to contribute to the successful delivery of world-class data centre infrastructure, we'd love to hear from you. Apply now to join CTS Group as our Commissioning Lead in Kvandal, Norway.
